references.text: The Lord commands Moses to send all lepers out of the camp, which expands on the regulation concerning isolating unclean persons outside the camp.
Miriam becomes leprous and must be kept outside the camp for seven days, a practical example of the law in Leviticus 13:46.
Four leprous men sit outside the city gate of Samaria, in accordance with the law that lepers had to live outside the camp.
King Uzziah became leprous and had to live in an isolated house, excluded from the temple of the Lord, fulfilling this law.
The preceding verses describe how a leper should behave and dress, as part of the same regulation on isolation.
Ten leprous men stand far away from Jesus and call out to him, showing that they followed the law requiring them to keep their distance from others.
Lamentations describes Jerusalem as unclean, living alone like a leper—a poetic image using language from the laws concerning leprosy.
